questions.cardText:
[Psychology] What is naive realism?
A. The assumption that one’s perception of reality is true and objective
B. The belief that reality is subjective
C. The theory that reality is naively constructed by society
Answer: A. Most people see the world from the perspective of naive realism without realizing it. Many interpersonal conflicts arise from it, as people often assume their perception is universally accurate.
questions.de: Wie nennt die Sozialpsychologie die Neigung zu glauben, man sehe die Welt objektiv, und wer anderer Meinung sei, müsse uninformiert, irrational oder voreingenommen sein?
questions.en: What does social psychology call the tendency to believe that we see the world objectively, and that people who disagree must be uninformed, irrational or biased?

timeline.labelEn: Lee Ross and Andrew Ward publish 'Naive realism in everyday life', framing the bias in social psychology
timeline.labelDe: Lee Ross und Andrew Ward veröffentlichen „Naive realism in everyday life“ und prägen damit den Begriff in der Sozialpsychologie

questions.notes: Reversed from 'what is naive realism' to ask the term. Distinct from naïve realism in the philosophy of perception.

questions.cardText:
[Physics] What is the theory that describes the behavior of objects moving at constant speeds approaching the speed of light?
A. Quantum mechanics
B. General relativity
C. Special relativity
Answer: C.
questions.de: Welche 1905 von Albert Einstein veröffentlichte Theorie beschreibt das Verhalten von Körpern, die sich mit konstanter Geschwindigkeit nahe der Lichtgeschwindigkeit bewegen?
questions.en: Which theory, published by Albert Einstein in 1905, describes the behaviour of objects moving at constant speeds approaching the speed of light?

timeline.labelEn: Albert Einstein publishes 'On the Electrodynamics of Moving Bodies', presenting special relativity
timeline.labelDe: Albert Einstein veröffentlicht „Zur Elektrodynamik bewegter Körper“ und stellt die spezielle Relativitätstheorie vor

questions.notes: Special relativity covers inertial (non-accelerating) frames; 'constant speeds' in the card is the key against general relativity.
